work_order.approach: Fix the one real defect at its source and pay down the two coverage debts in the same slice, with no UI component change. In lib/settle/actions.ts createPayment, after the existing endpoint-belongs-to-group check, load the group's current membership ids and refuse with a new explicit message when neither endpoint is current — placeholders count as current because their membership row exists (null userId is not the test; row existence is). lib/settle/actions.ts:102-107 accepts any id in the balances map, which includes departed participants per lib/settle/balances.ts:168-182; deletePayment at actions.ts:173-177 requires the viewer to be payer or recipient, which is impossible when both endpoints are departed and hold no session.

PR #22's five extra paths (groups-panels exports, groups/queries membershipId, settle/queries, settle/summary plus its test) are already-merged enabling code; amending that historical work order is not a code change.

Alongside it sit two coverage debts: a backwards test title hiding the true sender-up/recipient-down convention, and the missing mid-transaction failure case the last work order promised.

issue_snapshot.body:
What the review and QA of PR #22 (for #7) found and did not fix there — filed as it merged, one ticket for the lot.

## From the review

Non-blocking findings the reviewer approved despite: a statement about severity, not a judgement that they are wrong.

### Five changed paths sit outside the work order's files[] (groups-panels exports, groups/queries membershipId, settle/queries, settle/summary + its test); each is a justified enabling change, so the work order should be amended, not the code.

> Five changed paths sit outside the work order's files[] (groups-panels exports, groups/queries membershipId, settle/queries, settle/summary + its test); each is a justified enabling change, so the work order should be amended, not the code.
> 
> `lib/settle/summary.ts:1`
> 
> Evidence: gh pr view 22 files (22 paths) vs work-order.json files[]; diff sizes: groups-panels +18/-3 export-only, groups/queries +10, settle/queries +72 new, summary +135 new with +256 of tests
> 
> Fix: Amend work-order.json files[]/tests[] to list the five paths; leave code as is.

### balances.test.ts:328 names the payment-direction convention backwards ('recipient up, payer down'); its own assertions prove sender-up/recipient-down, matching the code.

> balances.test.ts:328 names the payment-direction convention backwards ('recipient up, payer down'); its own assertions prove sender-up/recipient-down, matching the code.
> 
> `lib/settle/balances.test.ts:328`
> 
> Evidence: PR ref balances.test.ts lines 328-352: Bo (sender) -1000 to 0, Ada (recipient) +2000 to 1000; code folds sent at +1, received at -1
> 
> Fix: Rename to 'moves the payer of a payment up and its recipient down, and settles the group'.

### A payment between two departed seats can be recorded but never deleted, stranding a mistaken write with no recourse.

> A payment between two departed seats can be recorded but never deleted, stranding a mistaken write with no recourse.
> 
> `lib/settle/actions.ts:173`
> 
> Evidence: createPayment accepts any two ids present in the computeNetBalances map (actions.ts:102-107), and that map includes departed ledger participants (balances.ts departed fold); simplifyDebts explicitly allows transfers naming departed holders and SettleUpForm offers every suggested transfer for recording. deletePayment then requires the acting current member to be the payer or the recipient (actions.ts:173-177) — but neither endpoint is a current member, a departed seat holds no session, and there is no owner override — so the delete is refused forever and the nets stay wrong.
> 
> Fix: Require at least one endpoint to be a current membership when creating a payment, or allow any current member to delete a payment whose endpoints are both departed.

### The work order's promised transaction-atomicity case for settle writes was not written: no test fails a payment write mid-transaction.

> The work order's promised transaction-atomicity case for settle writes was not written: no test fails a payment write mid-transaction.
> 
> `lib/settle/actions.test.ts`
> 
> Evidence: work-order.json tests for lib/settle/actions.test.ts list 'failing write leaves no payment and no activity row (transaction atomicity)'; the 711-line file (18 cases) proves refusals write nothing and proves create/delete round-trips, but grep for atomic/rollback/half-written/part-way finds nothing, while lib/expenses/actions.test.ts:692 proves the identical single-tx shape with a mid-write mock failure ('leaves nothing behind when the write fails part-way through'). The tx closure itself follows the proven pattern, so this is coverage debt, not a suspected half-write.
> 
> Fix: Add a mid-transaction failure test mirroring the expense one (throw between the payment insert and the activity insert, assert no payment and no activity rows remain).

---

**Check each one still reproduces before planning it.** They were written against the PR as it stood, and a later round can have fixed one. Some may not hold up: say so and drop them rather than implementing something that was never wrong. Split this if they turn out to be unrelated.
